subject: p95/p99 end-to-end latency qualification — hosted vs incumbent: post-demo notes and asks
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@ornyx.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — p95/p99 end-to-end numbers and clarification asks

Hi Aditi —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope a short technical probe: 

Summary of what we observed on the demo (hosted API vs incumbent):
- Redwood (hosted): end-to-end p95 ≈ 140ms, p99 ≈ 410ms for typical 256-token chat flows (streaming enabled, 8 concurrent streams in the demo harness).
- Incumbent: p95 ≈ 330ms, p99 ≈ 1.1s under the same demo harness and message sizes.

Notes/context: the hosted numbers above include network RTT from our test origin to regional POP and continuous batching effects disabled for low-latency probing. Streaming chunk size used was 64 tokens. These were synthetic replayed calls—your real traffic may differ.

Asks to scope a meaningful probe/PoC:
1) Traffic profile: can you share a 1-hour sample (anonymized) showing arrival rates, average tokens per request, streaming vs non-streaming percentages, and typical concurrency peaks? CSV or JSON is fine.
2) Target SLOs: you mentioned wanting p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500–600ms for the user-facing path — can you confirm the acceptable p99 upper bound?
3) Failure/fallback expectations: if the model variant falls back to a quantized variant under resource pressure, what are your acceptable latency and quality tradeoffs?
4) Security/operational asks: we'll share SOC2 and standard SOC2-hosted onboarding docs. Do you need an IP allowlist or specific audit log retention?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- If you can provide the traffic profile and confirm p99 target, we’ll propose a 2-hour probe window that replays representative traffic from your sample and measures end-to-end p95/p99 with streaming enabled.
- We'll attach a short concurrency matrix (CSV) and a one-page fallback summary for your review.

Attachments: streaming-concurrency-matrix.csv (CSV), redwood-streaming-fallback-summary.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick 30-min technical call once we have the sample.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@ornyx.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ornyx Platform Team <platform@ornyx.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — p95/p99 end-to-end numbers and clarification asks

Thanks Priyom — good summary and helpful numbers. A few items from our side: 

- Confirming target SLOs: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms for our main user-facing route (256–512 token outputs, streaming preferred). Anything above 600ms for p99 starts to introduce unacceptable UX regressions.
- Traffic sample: attaching a small anonymized CSV extract (separate secure upload link via our platform). The high-level profile: mean arrival rate 150 qps average, 450 qps 95th percentile burst, 2.5 tokens/request average, ~70% streaming-enabled. Peak concurrency historically hits ~320 concurrent inflight requests.
- We care about graceful degradation: if the primary variant is saturated, we prefer automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model (with comparable quality) rather than hitting a 503. We need to understand Redwood's fallback latency delta and how hedging/fanout would affect p99.

Questions for you: 
1) In the demo you mentioned prefix/KV caching — how much of the p95 win was due to warm KV caches versus pure compute/runtime speed?
2) For streaming, do you enforce a single TCP connection per session (we have a WebSocket gateway) or do you recommend short-lived HTTP/2 streams?

We can provide the traffic sample via the secure drive link if that works for you. Also happy to schedule the probe next week — Mar 22 or Mar 23 availability: mornings PT.

Regards,
Aditi Shah
Head of Platform, Ornyx
aditi.shah@ornyx.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@ornyx.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — p95/p99 end-to-end numbers and clarification asks

Aditi — appreciate the clarity and the targets. Quick answers and a concrete probe plan below.

Short answers:
- KV/prefix cache impact: in the demo ~20–30% of p95 improvement came from warm prefix/KV cache on repeated prompts. The remainder is serving runtime and network path. We'll design the probe to include both cold and warm scenarios so you get a realistic p99 tail.
- Streaming transport: we fully support HTTP/2 streaming and recommend keeping a single long-lived HTTP/2 stream per session for reduced connection overhead. We can also accept WebSocket ingress behind a gateway but suggest passthrough to HTTP/2 for the last-mile to minimize proxies.

Proposed probe (what Redwood will run):
1) Duration: 2 hours during a mutually agreed slot (we suggest Mar 23 09:00–11:00 PT).
2) Traffic shape: replay your provided sample with the following knobs:
   - Preserve streaming percentage (~70%).
   - Maintain observed burst patterns (95th percentile burst to 450 qps).
   - Inject cold-start windows at controlled intervals to measure cache effects.
3) Metrics we will report: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, per-chunk streaming latency distribution, tail error rates, concurrency vs queuing delay, and model fallback occurrences (if any).
4) Safety: we'll run the probe in a sandboxed account and produce logs/artifacts you can inspect. We will not persist raw user content — we can redact tokens for privacy.

Action items for Ornyx:
- Upload anonymized sample to https://drive.redwood.ai/s/ORX-POC-DATASET or share a signed URL.
- Confirm Mar 23 09:00 PT or propose alternate slot.
- Confirm fallback policy: allow automatic fallback to second-tier model with a latency delta up to +120ms for p95 but no more than +300ms for p99 (we will label these in the report).

Attachments: redwood-streaming-fallback-summary.pdf (one-pager describing fallback flow and expected deltas)

Next steps: if you confirm the slot and upload the sample, Ben and I will coordinate infra configuration and Marissa will own the result packet and ops checklist.

Thanks — looking forward.
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap — internal prep items for Ornyx probe

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the chain. Ornyx confirmed targets and provided a sample outline. Internal checklist before Mar 23 probe: 

- Ben: reserve a small dedicated pool (region: us-west-2) for Mar 23 09:00–11:00 PT. Need approx capacity for 450 qps bursts and 320 concurrent inflight. Plan: 4 x rtx-8000-equivalent nodes with autoscale buffer.
- Marissa: prepare the result packet template with p50/p95/p99, per-chunk streaming histograms, and a fallback-summary section. Include the SOC2 link (https://security.redwood.ai/soc2-report-2026.pdf).
- Both: bake a cold-cache run into the probe schedule (first 15 minutes of each hour) so Ornyx can see warm vs cold delta.
- Ops: ensure logging redact for user content and upload artifacts to drive.redwood.ai under ORX folder.

I'll book the Mar 23 09:00 PT slot tentatively and ask Ornyx to upload the sample by EOD Wed (Mar 17). If they push, we can move to Mar 24 morning.

Quick private notes: we should highlight streaming chunk-size impact and how our fallback hedging keeps visible error rates low. Also be ready to explain how quantized variants may increase p99 by ~80–150ms in worst case depending on sequence lengths.

Thanks — Priyom
